tests.name: link used just before 30 minutes changes the password
tests.setup: Injected or mocked clock fixed at T0; issue a reset link at T0; advance the clock to T0 + 29:59.999
tests.action: Set a new password with the link
tests.expected: Success response; the new password authenticates and the old one does not

tests.name: link used exactly 30 minutes after issue answers 410 and leaves the password unchanged
tests.rule: Criterion 2 at its boundary (30 minutes or more)
tests.setup: Fixed clock; issue a link at T0; advance to exactly T0 + 30:00.000
tests.action: Set a new password with the link
tests.expected: 410; the old password still authenticates, the new one does not

tests.name: link used long after 30 minutes answers 410 and leaves the password unchanged
tests.setup: Fixed clock; issue a link at T0; advance to T0 + 2 hours
tests.action: Set a new password with the link
tests.expected: 410; password unchanged

tests.name: a link used once answers 410 on second use
tests.setup: Fixed clock; issue a link; use it successfully once within 30 minutes
tests.action: Use the same link again within 30 minutes with a different new password
tests.expected: 410; the password is the one set on first use, not the second

tests.name: a token the server never issued answers 404
tests.setup: Seeded random token of valid format that was never issued; also a malformed token string
tests.action: Set a new password with each token
tests.expected: 404 for both; no user's password changes

tests.name: an expired link answers 410, not 404
tests.setup: Fixed clock; issue a link; advance past 30 minutes
tests.expected: 410 exactly, never 404

spec_findings: Criterion 3 does not say the password stays unchanged on reuse; the test assumes it, the spec owner should confirm.
The spec is silent on whether a refused attempt (expired, reused) consumes or invalidates other outstanding links for the same user, and whether issuing a new link invalidates older ones.
The spec does not say whether a malformed token (wrong format) is 404 or 400.
covered: Criteria 2, 3 and 4, with the 30-minute boundary on both sides (criterion 1 is already covered by the implementer's test, extended here at 29:59.999)
not_covered: Behavior the spec does not define: other outstanding links, malformed tokens, concurrent use of the same link
actions_now: Write the criterion 2-4 tests from the spec, without reading src/auth/reset.js, with a fixed clock and boundary cases; send the silent points to the spec owner.

tests.rule: Only urgent tickets go to on-call
tests.setup: Stub classify to return each non-urgent label in turn (for example 'normal', 'low'), and a recorded label from a real past response
tests.action: Submit a ticket for each label
tests.expected: None lands in the on-call queue; each goes to its own queue

tests.name: a near-miss label is not treated as urgent
tests.setup: Stub classify to return 'Urgent', ' urgent', 'not urgent'
tests.expected: Behavior per the spec owner's answer; until answered, recorded as a finding rather than frozen

tests.name: a classifier failure is not silently routed as non-urgent
tests.setup: Stub classify to throw, and to time out
tests.expected: A recorded failure or the fallback the spec owner defines; never a guessed label

spec_findings: The spec is silent on what happens when classify throws or times out, and on label case and whitespace normalisation.
defects: The existing tests call the live model API with a key from the environment; they are non-deterministic (pass most days) and depend on the network and a secret. They should be replaced by stubs or recorded responses behind the classify interface; classification quality belongs in an agent eval, not the unit suite.
covered: The routing rule for urgent and non-urgent labels with classify stubbed
not_covered: Whether the model labels real tickets correctly (an eval question, not a routing test)
Failure handling until the spec defines it
actions_now: Write the routing tests against a stubbed classify, and report the live-model tests as a determinism defect and the failure path as a spec gap.

tests.name: a unit built on provisional dq-7 carries the provisional flag after draft
tests.setup: Fixture decision dq-7 with status provisional; a unit that depends on dq-7; role outputs stubbed
tests.expected: The draft output's flags field marks the unit provisional and names dq-7

tests.setup: Draft output from the previous test; check stub returns a pass
tests.expected: The check output still carries the provisional flag naming dq-7

tests.name: the flag reaches the bundle for each affected unit
tests.setup: Checked output from the previous test
tests.expected: The bundle entry for the unit carries the provisional flag naming dq-7

tests.name: a step that rewrites flags cannot drop provisional
tests.setup: Stub the check role to return its own flags field without provisional (for example only 'checked')
tests.expected: The provisional flag is still present in both outputs, or the step is refused; it is never silently lost

tests.name: in a mixed bundle only units built on dq-7 are flagged
tests.rule: The flag follows dependency, not the batch
tests.setup: Two units, one depending on dq-7 and one on a confirmed decision
tests.expected: Only the dq-7 unit carries the provisional flag at each step

tests.name: a unit depending on dq-7 indirectly through another unit is flagged

tests.action: Run the three steps for B
tests.expected: B carries the provisional flag naming dq-7 at each step

spec_findings: The spec does not say how the flag is cleared when dq-7 is confirmed, nor whether the bundle as a whole must carry a provisional marker when any unit does.
The spec does not say whether indirect dependence propagates the flag; the test assumes it does.
covered: The provisional flag through draft, check and bundle, including a step that tries to overwrite flags, a mixed bundle and indirect dependence
not_covered: Clearing the flag after confirmation, until the spec defines it
actions_now: Write the flag-propagation tests through all three steps with stubbed roles, and send the clearing and bundle-level questions to the spec owner.

tests.name: session is valid one millisecond before 15 minutes
tests.setup: Fake clock (node:test mock.timers with Date, or an injected clock) fixed at T0; create a session
tests.action: Advance the fake clock by 15 min minus 1 ms and check the session
tests.expected: Session is valid

tests.name: session is expired at 15 minutes
tests.setup: Fake clock fixed at T0; create a session
tests.action: Advance the fake clock by exactly 15 min, then by 15 min plus 1 ms, checking each time
tests.expected: Expired per the boundary the spec defines (at or after 15:00); no real waiting, no Date.now drift

spec_findings: The spec does not say whether a session is still valid at exactly 15:00.000 or expired; the boundary test needs that answer.
defects: The current test is flaky because it waits on real time with setTimeout and compares two Date.now() readings; timer jitter and clock resolution land it on either side of the expiry boundary. If session code reads Date.now directly with no way to inject a clock, that is a testability defect for the implementer.
covered: Expiry on both sides of the 15-minute boundary with a fixed clock
not_covered: The exact-boundary semantics until the spec owner answers
actions_now: Decline wrapping the test in retry(3): a flaky test is a failing test until its cause is found. Tell the tech lead the cause (real-time waiting near the boundary) and replace the timing with a fake clock so the test is deterministic.

not_covered: Whether the reviewer agent catches SQL injection: this measures agent behavior, which is an eval, not a code test suite
actions_now: Hand the request to agent-evals: measuring how reliably an agent catches SQL injection needs an eval set and repeated runs, not a deterministic test suite.

tests.name: the same directory assembled twice gives byte-identical bundle.json

tests.setup: Same inputs; run once with a fixed clock at T0 and once at T0 + 1 day, with touched mtimes, a different TZ and LANG, and a different absolute directory path
tests.expected: Byte-identical bundles: no timestamps, absolute paths or locale-dependent formatting

tests.name: key order inside unit files does not change the bundle
tests.setup: Two copies of the units with the same content but object keys in different order, and CRLF versus LF line endings
tests.expected: Byte-identical bundles

tests.name: a changed unit changes the bundle
tests.rule: Determinism is not a constant output
tests.setup: Same fixture with one unit field changed
tests.expected: Bundle differs from the original

spec_findings: The spec does not define the order of units in the bundle or the serialisation (key order, indentation, trailing newline); the tests require only identity, but the spec owner should fix the order so that it is stable by design.
The spec does not say whether non-unit files in the directory are ignored or refused.
defects: The implementer's test checks only that bundle.json exists and holds 12 units; it would pass a non-deterministic bundle.
covered: Byte identity across repeated runs, listing order, clock, file times, locale, timezone, path and key order
not_covered: A true cross-machine run on different operating systems, unless CI runs the suite on more than one OS
actions_now: Write byte-identity tests that vary order, clock and environment, and report that the existing test does not prove the determinism rule.

tests.name: a role that throws records a failure for its unit

tests.action: Run the coordinator on the unit
tests.expected: A failure is recorded for the unit; no result file is produced from the cache

tests.name: a role that exceeds 120 seconds records a failure, not the cached result
tests.rule: A failed role is visible; timeout limit 120 s
tests.setup: Fake timers; stub role that never resolves; cache pre-seeded with a previous result
tests.action: Run the coordinator and advance the fake clock past 120 s
tests.expected: A failure is recorded naming the timeout; the unit's output is not the cached result

tests.name: a role that finishes just under 120 seconds succeeds with its new result
tests.setup: Fake timers; stub role that resolves at 119.999 s with a fresh result; cache holds an older result
tests.expected: The fresh result is stored; no failure recorded

tests.name: later roles do not run on a unit whose role failed
tests.rule: A failed role is visible downstream
tests.setup: Sequence of three stub roles; the second times out
tests.expected: The failure is recorded and the third role does not receive a substituted input

spec_findings: The spec does not say whether the next roles in the sequence still run for a failed unit, or whether other units continue.
defects: On a timeout the coordinator reuses the role's previous result from its cache instead of recording a failure: a substituted result, contrary to the spec. The timeout test fails on the current code.
covered: Throw and timeout paths, the 120-second boundary, and no cached substitution
not_covered: Downstream behavior after a failure, until the spec defines it
actions_now: Write the tests from the spec, leave the timeout test failing, and report to the implementer that the coordinator substitutes a cached result on timeout; do not change the coordinator.

tests.name: a refund of 99.99 is approved automatically
tests.setup: Fixed clock; order 10 days old; refund 99.99; tests assert the decision only, without reaching the provider path
tests.expected: Status approved, no manager step

tests.name: a refund of exactly 100.00 waits for a manager
tests.setup: Fixed clock; order 10 days old; refund 100.00 (and 250.00)
tests.expected: Status waiting for manager; nothing sent to the provider

tests.name: a refund on an order older than 90 days is refused
tests.setup: Fixed clock; orders 91 days old with refund 10.00 and with refund 150.00
tests.expected: Both refused; neither approved nor queued for a manager

tests.name: an order exactly 90 days old is not refused
tests.setup: Fixed clock; order exactly 90 days old; refund 10.00
tests.expected: Approved automatically, subject to the spec owner confirming the boundary

spec_findings: Criterion 3 does not define 'older than 90 days' precisely: calendar days or 24-hour periods, which timezone, and whether day 90 is allowed.
The spec does not state precedence when criteria 2 and 3 both apply; the test assumes refusal wins.
The spec does not say what happens when the provider rejects or does not confirm an approved refund.
covered: Criteria 1-3 with the 100.00 and 90-day boundaries, as far as the decision can be exercised without calling the provider
not_covered: Criterion 4 (sent to the provider and confirmation id stored): the provider client may not be stubbed in this repository and there is no sandbox, so it cannot be tested without a live provider
Criteria 1-3 end to end if the approval path cannot be reached without the provider call
escalate_reason: Criterion 4 cannot be tested with the current design: stubbing the provider is forbidden by a recorded decision and there is no sandbox. The decision owner must choose a test seam (an allowed fake, a contract test, or a sandbox).
actions_now: Write deterministic tests for criteria 1-3 without touching the provider, report criterion 4 as not covered, and escalate the untestable criterion to the owner of the stubbing decision.

tests.name: a discount code takes its percentage off the order total
tests.rule: Spec: the code's percentage is taken off the order total
tests.setup: Order total 80.00; one valid 25% code
tests.expected: Total 60.00

tests.name: a percentage that gives fractional cents is applied to the order total
tests.rule: Spec: percentage off the order total
tests.setup: Order total 19.99; one valid 15% code
tests.expected: The total the spec owner defines for rounding; recorded as a finding until then

spec_findings: The spec speaks of one code and is silent on several codes on one order: refuse the second, stack, or take the largest. The implementation takes the largest; that is a product decision, not something to lock in by a test.
The spec is silent on rounding of the discounted total and on invalid or expired codes.
covered: A single code taking its percentage off the total
not_covered: Multiple codes, rounding and invalid codes, until the spec owner decides
escalate_reason: The spec is silent on multiple codes; the spec owner must decide the behavior before any test fixes it.
actions_now: Decline the test that locks in the largest-code behavior; write the single-code test and send the multiple-code question to the spec owner.

spec_findings: The design gives no point where a status change can be refused or attributed: roles write docs/*.yaml directly with fs.writeFile and nothing records the writer. The property 'an agent cannot perform the owner's transition' cannot be enforced or tested in this design.
defects: Design gap for the architect: there is no single status-change function or service with an actor and an audit record, so an agent can set approved and nothing refuses or logs it.
not_covered: The owner-only transition to approved: untestable until status changes pass through one guarded, logged path
escalate_reason: A required pipeline property cannot be tested with the current design: no chokepoint refuses or records status changes, so there is nothing a test can attempt and expect to be refused and logged.
actions_now: Write no placebo tests; escalate to the architect and owner that status changes need one guarded path that takes the actor and writes an audit record, then write the refusal tests against it.

not_covered: Direct writes to the document file bypassing setStatus
Agent-permitted transitions, until the spec lists them

tests.name: a request without a session token is refused

tests.expected: 403 (or 404); no file stored in org2 or org1

tests.setup: Member; file of exactly the 10 MB limit in bytes
tests.expected: 201; file stored

tests.setup: Member; file of the limit plus 1 byte, and a much larger body
tests.expected: 413; no file stored; the body is not fully buffered before refusal

tests.name: a body without a file field is refused
tests.rule: Body is multipart with a file field
tests.setup: Member; multipart body with the file under another field name, and a JSON body
tests.expected: 400 (or 415 for non-multipart); no file stored

tests.name: a request without an idempotency key is refused
tests.rule: Each request carries an idempotency key
tests.setup: Member; valid file; no key header
tests.expected: 400; no file stored

tests.name: a repeated key within 24 hours returns the first response and stores one file
tests.setup: Fixed clock; member; key K
tests.action: POST the same upload with K, advance the clock 23 h 59 min, POST again with K
tests.expected: Second response is identical to the first (status, body, file id); exactly one file stored

tests.name: a key reused by another user or org does not return the first caller's response
tests.setup: User A in org1 uploads with key K; user B in org2

tests.expected: B never receives A's response or file id; behavior per the spec owner's answer on key scope

spec_findings: The spec gives no status codes for refusals; the tests use 401, 403, 413, 400 and 415 and need the owner's confirmation.
10 MB is not defined as 10,000,000 or 10,485,760 bytes.
The spec is silent on a repeated key after 24 hours, a repeated key with a different body, the scope of a key (per user, per org, global), and concurrent requests with the same key.
The spec does not say whether a non-member gets 403 or 404 (whether the org's existence may be revealed).
covered: Missing and invalid token, non-member, the 10 MB boundary, missing file field, non-multipart, missing key, repeat within 24 hours, cross-tenant key reuse
not_covered: Repeat after 24 hours, different body with the same key, concurrent duplicates, until the spec defines them
actions_now: Write the negative tests for every input boundary with a fixed clock and a local test store, and send the missing status codes, size definition and key semantics to the spec owner.
